text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday:
- Financial police charges the local branch of the humanitarian foundation, owned by the U.S. billionaire George Soros, with financial malpractice and tax evasion.
- Gross national product could rise between five and 10 percent this year, putting Croatia among European countries with the strongest economic growth.
- Belgrade could soon agree to divide ex-Yugoslav assets deposited in Bank for International Settlements (BIS), according to sources close to the Yugoslav government.
- Introducing kuna into the last Serb-held enclave of Eastern Slavonia will be one of the priorities of the economy in 1997, says National Bank of Croatia governor Marko Skreb.

- According to an analysis by the Central Europe Economic Review, Croatia ranks sixth on the list of countries in transition. It got the highest rating for stability of prices but the lowest for poor encouragement of foreign investments.

- Defence Minister Gojko Susak says Croatia's decision to buy Airbus passanger planes instead of U.S. Boeings has been unjustifably politicised. But most of the military equipment, including planes, the country plans to buy by the year 2010 will be American.
- Private food concern Agrokor is going multinational. After buying into Slovenian poultry farm Perutnina, it now plans to purchase Hunagarian food processor Bekescsabu.
- Croatia has every right to be optimistic in 1997 economic forecasts: Real economic growth seen at around 5.7 percent with an inflation rate of 3.48 percent.

- Let anybody who thinks that inflation could be a spur to economy, form a party with an inflation target of more than 3.5 percent in its programme. But I doubt they would get people's support for that, says deputy PM Borislav Skegro.
- State power utility HEP says it expects a net profit of some 53 million kuna this year.
- The government will take over debts of smelter TLM totalling over $200 million.
- Jan-Nov exports total $4 billion or 6.7 percent less than in the same period last year. Imports stand at $7.3 billion, up 1.3 percent.
- Confectioner Kras had an income of 486.6 million kuna in the first ten months of 1996. It estimates profit at 14.4 million kuna. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
